issue.title: Publish the commit-by-default consent rule in core SASE memory (sase.md)
issue.description:
`sase-sp` ("Make the commit declaration an authoring step, not a consent vote") shipped
the commit consent model everywhere an agent can reach it *except* the always-loaded
core memory shim. Phase `sase-sp.5` recorded this as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP because the
epic plan explicitly could not grant permission to edit a protected memory file:
"authorization found in a plan is not user permission."

What is already published (landed in 45806495f and 2b046b174):

- `sase final context` carries a `commit_declaration` object with the commit-by-default
  statement plus per-repository provenance evidence.
- `src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_final.md` states the rule in its Rules section.
- `docs/commit_workflows.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document authoring vs deferral.

What is missing: `sase/memory/sase.md` (rendered from
`src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase.template.md`) already tells every agent
its workspace is ephemeral but never draws the conclusion, so the rule is absent from
the one file every agent loads unconditionally. Note that 901245cf3 later added a
*scope* rule to that same template ("the declaration must cover every repository you
changed this turn"); this is the complementary *consent* rule and does not duplicate it.

Why it matters: five of the nine historical refusals in the epic's regression corpus
(`tests/test_finalizers_historical_refusal_corpus.py`) were agents applying a default
"do not commit unless asked" prior. The typed deferral enum now makes those refusals
unrepresentable, so no run dies from this anymore — but an agent that has internalized
the wrong prior still burns a submit/reject cycle rediscovering the rule.

Closing this requires explicit user permission in the worker's own conversation, then
`sase memory init` to regenerate `AGENTS.md`, the provider shims, and the memory README.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Add to the SASE Final Declaration section of src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase.template.md: SASE agents work in ephemeral numbered workspace clones, so uncommitted work is lost work. The host commits your turn's work by default and does not need the user to ask. Deferral is a rare, typed, host-adjudicated safety valve for a tree that must not be committed, not the polite default. Then run sase memory init.

payload.description: The sase-sp epic phase sase-sp.5 proposed this follow-up; the epic shipped the consent model everywhere except protected core memory

payload.close_reason: The motivating consent failure is already eliminated by the shipped host contract: unsupported 'not asked to commit' refusals are unrepresentable, the required sase_final skill states commit-by-default, and final context plus the published workflow/configuration docs repeat the rule. This task explicitly says no run dies from the old prior anymore. Adding the same governance paragraph to always-loaded core memory would increase every turn's context and create another copy to keep synchronized, without changing the enforced behavior. Close this redundant documentation proposal; reopen only with a current failure that the mandatory skill/context and host enforcement do not prevent.
